While I'm a long time linux user I'm somehow still new to the systemd debacle. Having done some research over the past few days it looks like a slow motion trainwreck (binary log files seem like a bad enough idea, that it appears to consolidate much of the OS into a single monolithic entity seems even worse) and I'd like to pick a distro that will avoid adopting it, or at the very least allow me to avoid adopting it by supporting alternatives like runit, upstart, etc.

Anyway, I'd been considering going with Mint since it seems to be treading the "we support both" path for the moment, but I have long-term concerns about that.

So, has anyone here used Void and what did they think of it?

Installation was easy. I heard some people complaining that they couldn't get it working. It's just as easy as installing Debian, especially if you get one of the LiveCD versions pre-loaded with a desktop environment. The only issue is if you want something like LVM+LUKS, which makes it more like an Arch or Gentoo install process but they have a guide for that.

Once you get past that it's a young but solid distro. OpenRC is by far my favorite init software. An early adapter of LibreSSL as well. Comes with next to no software just like Arch so you can completely customize it from the ground up. This is great for intermediate to advanced users. My main gripe is that the repo is lacking but it's quickly swelling in size. Back when I installed it I had to compile Icecat myself, which is always a turn-off (it is available now though). There's also the issue of the packages being very granular, as I heard it described once. Check your packages before you install them. What may be included in one or two packages in any other distro's repo is spread across several in Void, which gives you greater choice but causes greater inconvenience. Also xbps-src is not even an application, just a bunch of build scripts. I expected to just type in a package name into a command like emerge and it would spit something out. Very disappointed in that.

Overall I think it's slowly shaping up to be a solid systemd-free competitor to Arch. It's definitely usable now and will soon be the standard, I think.
